verses.zh: 「这是耶和华―你们　神所吩咐教训你们的诫命、律例、典章，使你们在所要过去得为业的地上遵行，
verses.en: Now these are the commandments,[NOTE:1] statutes, and ordinances that the Lord your God instructed me to teach you so that you may carry them out in the land where you are headed[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “commandment.” The word מִצְוָה (mitsvah) again is in the singular, serving as a comprehensive term for the whole stipulation section of the book. See note on the word “commandments” in 5:31.
Heb “where you are going over to possess it” (so NASB); NRSV “that you are about to cross into and occupy.”
verses.commentary:
6:1 "the commandment, the statutes and the judgments" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: TERMS FOR GOD'S REVELATION.

▣ "the Lord your God" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, C. and D.

▣ "teach. . .do" Deuteronomy 6, along with the conclusion of chapter 5, could be characterized as a strenuous
emphasis on the need for obedience (cf. Deut. 5:29,31,32,33; 6:1,2,3,4,17,24, and 25).

This same emphasis on the need for obedience is repeated in the NT (cf. Luke 6:46; John 14:15,21,23;
15:10; James 2:14-26; 1 John 2:5; 5:2-3). One way that we show God that we really love Him is that we do what He has told us to do.
The focus of this obedience is directed first toward God and then toward our covenant brother/sister. God always takes the initiative
in grace (covenant benefits), yet He expects us to obey His covenant requirements! This is true of both the OT and NT. The NT requirements are

- faith (see SPECIAL TOPIC: FAITH, BELIEVE, OR TRUST)

- repentance (see SPECIAL TOPIC: REPENTANCE [NT])

- obedience(see SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP)

- service

- perseverance (see SPECIAL TOPIC: PERSEVERANCE)

- worship (see SPECIAL TOPIC: WORSHIP)

▣ "in the land where you are going to possess it" This of course, refers to Gen. 12:1-3. In the OT the
"land" aspect of the Abrahamic promise is emphasized while in the NT the "seed" aspect of the Abrahamic promise
is emphasized (tribe of Judah, family of Jesse, line of David).

SPECIAL TOPIC: POSSESS THE LAND

verses.zh: 好叫你和你子子孙孙一生敬畏耶和华―你的　神，谨守他的一切律例诫命，就是我所吩咐你的，使你的日子得以长久。
verses.en: and that you may so revere the Lord your God that you will keep all his statutes and commandments[NOTE:1] that I am giving[NOTE:2] you—you, your children, and your grandchildren—all your lives, to prolong your days.
notes: Here the terms are not the usual חֻקִּים (khuqqim) and מִשְׁפָּטִים (mishpatim; as in v. 1) but חֻקֹּת (khuqqot, “statutes”) and מִצְוֹת (mitsvot, “commandments”). It is clear that these terms are used interchangeably and that their technical precision ought not be overly stressed.
Heb “commanding.” For stylistic reasons, to avoid redundancy, “giving” has been used in the translation.
verses.commentary:
6:2 "so that you and your son and your grandson might fear the Lord your God" This
concept of family reverence and worship is emphasized in Deuteronomy (cf. Deut. 4:9-10; 5:29; 6:13,20-25; 11:19; 32:46). It is the
theological opposite of Deut. 5:9!

▣ "fear. . .keep" The reverence (BDB 431, KB 432, Qal IMPERFECT; see note at Deut. 5:10) is
demonstrated in "keeping" (BDB 1036, KB 1581, Qal INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT) all His covenant requirements!

SPECIAL TOPIC: FEAR (OT)

SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP

▣ "all the days of your life" Notice that this is an emphasis on lifestyle-daily obedience, not just particular
worship periods or annual feasts. Biblical faith is initial faith and repentance followed by lifestyle faith and repentance
(cf. Mark 1:15; Acts 3:16,19; 20:21). The Great Commission of Matt. 28:18-20 emphasizes a "discipleship" not only
a past "decision" (i.e. religious act).

▣ "that your days may be prolonged" This phrase has often been interpreted in connection with
Deut. 5:16 as a promise of individual longevity to those who honor their parents. However, because of the repeated
use of this phrase in Deut. 4:40; 5:16,33; 6:2; 11:9, it is obviously an idiom for the promise of a stable society, not
individual longevity. God's covenant is designed to promote a godly, stable, healthy, productive society
(cf. Deut. 6:3; and full note at Deut. 4:40).

SPECIAL TOPIC: HUMAN AGING

verses.zh: 以色列啊，你要听，要谨守遵行，使你可以在那流奶与蜜之地得以享福，人数极其增多，正如耶和华―你列祖的　神所应许你的。
verses.en: Pay attention, Israel, and be careful to do this so that it may go well with you and that you may increase greatly in number[NOTE:1]—as the Lord, the God of your ancestors,[NOTE:2] said to you, you will have a land flowing with milk and honey.
notes: Heb “may multiply greatly” (so NASB, NRSV); the words “in number” have been supplied in the translation for clarity.
Heb “fathers” (also in vv. 10, 18, 23).
verses.commentary:
6:3 Notice how the VERBS and concepts are repeated again and again.

▣ "that it may be well with you" This parallels the phrase, "that your days may be prolonged," of Deut. 6:2. Notice
the phrase is also found in Deut. 5:33; 15:16; 19:13

▣ "that you may multiply greatly. . ." It needs to be stated that
YHWH's basic method of attracting the nations to Himself was to bless Israel in a unique way. However, Israel's disobedience
never allowed this scenario to become effective. The cursing and blessing section of Leviticus 26 and Deuteronomy 27-29 is pivotal in
understanding the history of the children of Abraham. They were told specifically of the abundance that would accrue to
them if they would follow God and the cursing that would accrue to them if they disobeyed. The history of Israel is one of disobedience.

▣ "land flowing with milk and honey" This is a technical phrase in Ugaritic, Assyrian, and Egyptian
documents to denote Palestine. It is used often (cf. Exod. 3:8,17; 13:5; 33:3; Lev. 20:24; Num. 13:27; 14:8; 16:13; Deut. 6:3;
11:9; 26:9; 27:3; 31:20).

The Hebrew term "honey" (BDB 185) usually refers to sweet syrup made from fruit (cf. Deut. 6:3; 11:9; 26:9,15; 27:3; 31:20; and
Exod. 3:8,17), not bees. Beekeeping was not known in Palestine in this period, although wild bees making honey in rock cravasses was known.

Often, this syrup from fruit was added to wine to make it have a higher alcohol level (i.e. strong drink).

SPECIAL TOPIC: STUBBORNNESS

verses.zh: 「以色列啊，你要听！耶和华―我们　神是独一的主。
verses.en: Hear, O Israel: The Lord is our God, the Lord is one![NOTE:1]
notes: Verses 4-5 constitute the so-called Shema (after the first word שְׁמַע, shemaʿ, “hear”), widely regarded as the very heart of Jewish confession and faith. When Jesus was asked what was the greatest commandment of all, he quoted this text (Matt 22:37-38). tn Heb “the Lord, our God, the Lord, one.” (1) One option is to translate: “The Lord is our God, the Lord alone” (cf. NAB, NRSV, NLT). This would be an affirmation that the Lord was the sole object of their devotion. This interpretation finds support from the appeals to loyalty that follow (vv. 5, 14). (2) Another option is to translate: “The Lord is our God, the Lord is unique.” In this case the text would be affirming the people’s allegiance to the Lord, as well as the Lord’s superiority to all other gods. It would also imply that he is the only one worthy of their worship. Support for this view comes from parallel texts such as Deut 7:9 and 10:17, as well as the use of “one” in Song 6:8-9, where the starstruck lover declares that his beloved is unique (literally, “one,” that is, “one of a kind”) when compared to all other women.
verses.commentary:
6:4-5 See SPECIAL TOPIC: THE GREATEST COMMANDMENT

6:4 "Hear" This is the Hebrew VERB shema (BDB 1033, KB 1570). It means "to hear so as
to do." This is the focus of biblical covenant. The usage of this VERB in Deuteronomy implies that it was
used liturgically at set worship times (e.g. Deut. 4:1; 5:1; 9:1; 20:3; 27:9-10).

This prayer recorded in Deut. 6:4-6, (since the days of the second temple, 516 B.C.), is repeated even
to this day by Jewish people in both the morning and evening and at every worship occasion. It is their central confession of faith. However,
as the Jewish Study Bible, p. 379, points out, this text is not highlighted or emphasized in its original biblical context. Nor is it quoted in liturgical
prayers recorded in the OT.

Deuteronomy has several warnings related to this prayer (i.e. Deut. 4:1,2,6,9,13,14,15,19,23,26; also note
Micah 1:2; 3:1; 6:1). To hear God's revelation and not respond appropriately is a real problem (i.e. Luke 6:46; James 1:22-25;
2:14-26). Selfish living is a major spiritual problem. Knowledge brings responsibility (i.e. Luke 12:48)!

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP

▣

NASB, NKJV, NET, NIV, LXX
"the Lord is one"

NRSV, TEV, JPSOA
"the Lord alone"

NJB
"the only Yahweh"

REB
"the Lord our one God"

There is no VERB. This is the central theological pillar of the Israelites' affirmation of
monotheism (although it must be admitted that this central theological truth is not contextually highlighted; see
SPECIAL TOPIC: MONOTHEISM). Israel was very distinct from the
polytheism of her neighbors and especially the Canaanites' emphasis on the pantheon of fertility worship.

Notice how Paul uses this concept in Rom. 3:29-30, thereby combining YHWH's love for both Jew and Gentile (cf. Rom. 10:12).

SPECIAL TOPIC: FERTILITY WORSHIP OF THE ANE

verses.zh: 你要尽心、尽性、尽力爱耶和华―你的　神。
verses.en: You must love[NOTE:1] the Lord your God with your whole mind,[NOTE:2] your whole being,[NOTE:3] and all your strength.[NOTE:4]
notes: The verb אָהֵב (ʾahev, “to love”) in this setting communicates not so much an emotional idea as one of covenant commitment. To love the Lord is to be absolutely loyal and obedient to him in every respect, a truth Jesus himself taught (cf. John 14:15). See also the note on the word “loved” in Deut 4:37.
Heb “heart.” In OT physiology the heart (לֵב, לֵבָב; levav, lev) was considered the seat of the mind or intellect, so that one could think with one’s heart. See A. Luc, NIDOTTE 2:749-54.

Heb “soul”; “being.” Contrary to Hellenistic ideas of a soul that is discrete and separate from the body and spirit, OT anthropology equated the “soul” (נֶפֶשׁ, nefesh) with the person himself. It is therefore best in most cases to translate נֶפֶשׁ (nefesh) as “being” or the like. See H. W. Wolff, Anthropology of the Old Testament, 10-25; D. Fredericks, NIDOTTE 3:133-34.
For NT variations on the Shema see Matt 22:37-39; Mark 12:29-30; Luke 10:27.
verses.commentary:
6:5 "and you shall love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul
and with all your might" This is a strong emphasis which asserts that a faithful follower's response to God is to
involve the entire person. Jesus used this same verse in combination with Lev. 19:18 to affirm the entire essence
of the law (cf. Matt. 22:36-38; Mark 12:29-34; Luke 10:27-38).

Believers' "love" (BDB 12, KB 17 Qal PERFECT with waw) is assumed. It is characteristic
of Deuteronomy to link obedience to YHWH's covenant as evidence of one's love for Him (cf. Deut. 5:10; 6:5; 7:9; 10:12;
11:1,13; 13:3; 19:9; 30:6,16,20). See full note at Deut. 5:10 and
SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S COVENANT REQUIREMENTS OF ISRAEL.

The terms "heart" and "soul" are often used together to show the complete person (cf. Deut. 4:29;
10:12; 11:13; 13:3; 26:16; 30:2,6,10).

The term "soul" (BDB 659) describes the life-force (i.e. breath) in both humans and animals
(e.g. Gen. 1:20-30; 2:7,19; 7:22; Job 34:14-15; Ps. 104:29,30; 146:4; Eccl. 3:19-21). Here it refers to passionate desire. See
full notes on nephesh at Gen. 35:18 and Lev. 17:11; also SPECIAL TOPIC: NEPHESH.

"Might" (BDB 547) means "abundance" or "strength" (cf. 2 Kgs. 23:25). These three terms
"heart," "soul," "might," represent the complete person and is, therefore, parallel to the phrase, "with a whole
heart." Notice the term "all" (BDB 481) is repeated three times for emphasis.

This commandment is highlighted by Jesus as the greatest of the commandments
(cf. Matt. 22:34-40; Mark 12:29-30; Luke 10:25-37). Each of these is addressed to different types of Jewish leaders.
However, it must be understood that the life of Jesus and the Apostles was a transition period from the OT to the
NT. These two laws, love God (Deut. 6:5) and love your brother (Lev. 19:18) are surely also summaries of the new
covenant (cf. Jer. 31:31-34; Ezek. 36:22-36)!

For the question, "how should NT believers respond?" to OT laws see:

- How to Read the Bible for All Its Worth, Douglas Stuart, pp. 165-169

- Cracking Old Testament Codes, D. Brent Sandy and Ronald L. Giese, pp. 123-125

- SPECIAL TOPIC: PAUL'S VIEWS OF THE MOSAIC LAW

- SPECIAL TOPIC: MOSAIC LAW AND THE CHRISTIAN

verses.zh: 我今日所吩咐你的话都要记在心上，
verses.en: These words I am commanding you today must be kept in mind,
verses.commentary:
6:6 "these words" "These words" refer to YHWH's covenant, which was given through Moses.

▣ "shall be on your heart" The heart (BDB 523), in Hebrew, signifies the directing focus of
an individual's life (mind, will, emotions). The emphasis in the OT was also meant to be internal faithfulness, as in the NT
(cf. Deut. 4:29; 6:5, 6; 10:12; 11:13,18; 13:3; 26:16; 30:2, 6, 10; NT, "with all your mind," Mark 12:30; Luke 10:27).
We sometimes make a false distinction between the Old Covenant being an external law and the New Covenant
being internal faith. We probably get this fallacy from Jer. 31:31-34, which emphasizes "a new heart." However,
even in the OT, the individual believer was expected to direct his entire person, actions and motives toward the
Lord his God (i.e. Deut. 10:16).

SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP

SPECIAL TOPIC: HEART

verses.zh: 也要殷勤教训你的儿女。无论你坐在家里，行在路上，躺下，起来，都要谈论。
verses.en: and you must teach[NOTE:1] them to your children and speak of them as you sit in your house, as you walk along the road,[NOTE:2] as you lie down, and as you get up.
notes: Heb “repeat” (so NLT). If from the root I שָׁנַן (shanan), the verb means essentially to “engrave,” that is, “to teach incisively” (Piel); note NAB “Drill them into your children.” Cf. BDB 1041-42 s.v.
Or “as you are away on a journey” (cf. NRSV, TEV, NLT); NAB “at home and abroad.”
verses.commentary:
6:7 "you shall teach them diligently to your sons" The VERB (BDB 1041, KB 1606, Piel
PERFECT with waw) means "to sharpen" and in Piel this is the only usage. The term in Ugaritic means
"to repeat." That seems to be the basic emphasis of this verse. The rabbis use this verse to assert that the Shema
should be "repeated" morning and evening. We are to talk about God's will for our lives during the entire scope of
daily activities. It is the responsibility of parents to pass on lifestyle faith (cf. Deut. 4:9; 6:20-25; 11:19; 32:46, see full
note at Deut. 4:9). It is interesting that the flow of these different times for teaching falls into the same literary pattern
as Ps. 139:2-6 and Prov. 6:20-22. This emphasis on parental responsibility is repeated in Prov. 22:6. Our modern day
church school cannot take the place of parental training but it surely can supplement it!

verses.zh: 也要系在手上为记号，戴在额上为经文；
verses.en: You should tie them as a reminder on your forearm[NOTE:1] and fasten them as symbols[NOTE:2] on your forehead.
notes: Tie them as a sign on your forearm. Later Jewish tradition referred to the little leather containers tied to the forearms and foreheads as tefillin. They were to contain the following passages from the Torah: Exod 13:1-10, 11-16; Deut 6:5-9; 11:13-21. The purpose was to serve as a “sign” of covenant relationship and obedience.

Fasten them as symbols on your forehead. These were also known later as tefillin (see previous note) or phylacteries (from the Greek term). These box-like containers, like those on the forearms, held the same scraps of the Torah. It was the hypocritical practice of wearing these without heartfelt sincerity that caused Jesus to speak scathingly about them (cf. Matt 23:5).
verses.commentary:
6:8 "you shall bind them as a sign on your hand and they shall be as frontals on your forehead" Originally this
phrase seems to be used as imagery (cf. LXX). The context is lifestyle teaching opportunities for God's word. However, the
rabbis took this verse very literally and they began to wrap a leather strap around their left hand with a small box
(tefillin) attached which contained selected Scriptures from the Torah. The same kind of box was also strapped to
their forehead. These "phylacteries" or "frontals" (BDB 377) are also mentioned in Deut. 11:18 and Matt. 23:5.

verses.zh: 又要写在你房屋的门框上，并你的城门上。」
verses.en: Inscribe them on the doorframes of your houses and gates.[NOTE:1]
notes: The Hebrew term מְזוּזֹת (mezuzot) refers both to the door frames and to small cases attached on them containing scripture texts (always Deut 6:4-9 and 11:13-21; and sometimes the decalogue; Exod 13:1-10, 11-16; and Num 10:35-36). See J. H. Tigay, Deuteronomy (JPSTC), 443-44.
verses.commentary:
6:9 "And you shall write them on the doorposts of your house and on your gates" This again is a symbolic
gesture that God is to have a part, not only in our home life, but in our social life (i.e. gate, cf. Deut. 21:19; 22:15,24). As
the threshold (BDB 265) of the home was often seen as the place of the demonic in the Greek and Roman worlds, in
the Jewish world it represented the presence of God (i.e. the place where the blood of the Passover was placed,
cf. Exod. 12:7,22,23).

"Your gates" (BDB 1044) may refer to the place of social meeting and justice (i.e. like the city
gates). Usually, these small boxes and door markers (mezuza) contained several set passages of Scripture:
Deut. 6:4-9; 11:13-21 and Exod. 13:1-10,11-16.

verses.zh: 「耶和华―你的　神领你进他向你列祖亚伯拉罕、以撒、雅各起誓应许给你的地。那里有城邑，又大又美，非你所建造的；
verses.en: Then when the Lord your God brings you to the land he promised your ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob to give you—a land with large, fine cities you did not build,
verses.commentary:
6:10-11 This shows that Israel was going to possess the land of the Canaanites (cf. Gen. 15:16). She
would take over their homes, fields and vineyards. Yet, Deut. 6:12 emphasizes that she was not to forget that it
was the Lord who provided these and not her own resources (cf. Deut. 4:9; 8:11-20; Ps. 103:2). If they forgot
YHWH the reverse would occur. They would lose their homes, fields, and vineyards (cf. Deut. 28:27-48). Divine
love started the covenant relationship, but human obedience maintained it!!

SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP

verses.zh: 有房屋，装满各样美物，非你所装满的；有凿成的水井，非你所凿成的；还有葡萄园、橄榄园，非你所栽种的；你吃了而且饱足。
verses.en: houses filled with choice things you did not accumulate, hewn-out cisterns you did not dig, and vineyards and olive groves you did not plant—and you eat your fill,

verses.zh: 那时你要谨慎，免得你忘记将你从埃及地、为奴之家领出来的耶和华。
verses.en: be careful not to forget the Lord who brought you out of Egypt, that place of slavery.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “out of the house of slavery” (so NASB, NRSV).
verses.commentary:
6:12 "watch yourself" The VERB (BDB 1036, KB 1581, Niphal IMPERATIVE) is
used often in Deuteronomy, but usually in the Qal stem. The Niphal is found in Deut. 2:4; 4:9,15,23; 6:12; 8:6,11;
11:16; 12:13,19,30; 15:9; 23:9; 24:8 and usually with the sense of "be careful"!

SPECIAL TOPIC: CONSEQUENCES OF IDOLATRY

▣ "lest you forget" The VERB (BDB 1013, KB 1489, Qal IMPERFECT) is a
recurrent warning in Deuteronomy (cf. Deut. 4:9,23,31; 6:12; 8:11,14,19[twice]; 9:7; 25:19).

▣ "the Lord who brought you from this land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery" This
is the continuing emphasis of the book of Deuteronomy that YHWH's grace came to Israel first (cf. Deut. 4:10; 5:29; 6:2). It is unfortunate
to characterize the OT as law and the NT as grace (Martin Luther).

verses.zh: 你要敬畏耶和华―你的　神，事奉他，指着他的名起誓。
verses.en: You must revere the Lord your God, serve him, and take oaths using only his name.
verses.commentary:
6:13 This verse gives several things that Israel should do in relation to YHWH when they victoriously enter the Promised Land:

- "fear only the Lord your God" ‒ BDB 431, KB 432, Qal IMPERFECT

- "worship Him" ‒ BDB 712, KB 773 (lit. "serve"), Qal IMPERFECT

- "swear by His name" ‒ BDB 989, KB 1396, Niphal IMPERFECT. See full note at Deut. 5:11.

All of these involve worship and are used often in Moses' writings.

Part of the cultic worship of Israel was to make statements in the name of YHWH. Jesus seems to
quote this verse in Matt. 4:10 in His confrontation with the Evil One. He changes the word "fear" in Deut. 6:13 to the
word "worship," which shows us that these two terms are basically synonymous. The name of God reflected His
character and person.

SPECIAL TOPIC: CALL ON HIS NAME

SPECIAL TOPIC: WORSHIP

verses.zh: 不可随从别神，就是你们四围国民的神；
verses.en: You must not go after other gods, those[NOTE:1] of the surrounding peoples,
notes: Heb “from the gods.” The demonstrative pronoun has been used in the translation for stylistic reasons to avoid redundancy.
verses.commentary:
6:14 This verse adds another requirement to the list of Deut. 6:13:

"shall not follow other gods" ‒ BDB 229, KB 246, Qal IMPERFECT.

Here, the worship of Canaanite fertility gods is strictly forbidden.

SPECIAL TOPIC: IDOLATRY

▣ "gods. . .gods" These are the terms Elohim (BDB 43) and El (BDB 43). Here, these terms
are used of pagan gods.

SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, A. and C.

verses.zh: 因为在你们中间的耶和华―你　神是忌邪的　神，惟恐耶和华―你　神的怒气向你发作，就把你从地上除灭。
verses.en: for the Lord your God, who is present among you, is a jealous God—his anger will erupt against you and remove you from the land.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “lest the anger of the Lord your God be kindled against you and destroy you from upon the surface of the ground.” Cf. KJV, ASV “from off the face of the earth.”
verses.commentary:
6:15 "for the Lord your God in the midst of you" This was the purpose of creation. God
wants to dwell with those made in His image and likeness (cf. Gen. 1:26-27; 3:8). This is the Messianic concept of Immanuel,
which means "God with us" (cf. Isa. 7:14 and Matt. 28:20).

▣ "jealous God" This Hebrew term can mean "zealous" or "jealous" (BDB 888, cf. Deut. 4:24; 5:9; see
note at Deut. 4:24). Jealousy is a love word. We are only jealous of those for whom we have a deep, abiding love. This
is another affirmation of the love of God anthropomorphically stated in human, family terms.

SPECIAL TOPIC: JEALOUS. . .ZEALOUS

SPECIAL TOPIC: GOD DESCRIBED AS HUMAN (anthropomorphism)

▣ "the anger of the Lord your God will be kindled against you and He will
wipe you off the face of the earth" As revelatory as the love of God is, the same book reveals the wrath of God. The
same book that overwhelms us with His love shocks us with His anger.

- "kindled" BDB 354, KB 351, Qal IMPERFECT, cf. Deut. 11:16-17; 31:16-17; Jdg. 2:14; 6:13

- "wipe off" or "exterminate" BDB 1029, KB 1552, Hiphil PERFECT with waw, cf. Deut. 1:27; 2:22; 9:20; Josh. 9:24)

A good way to understand the relationship between God's love and His wrath is to compare Deut. 5:9 with 7:9.
As God does visit lifestyle sins from father to son to the third and fourth generations, He visits the blessing of faith to the thousandth
generations of those who love Him. God's love spurned is God's wrath. Isaiah calls God's wrath "His strange work" (cf. Isa. 28:21).

SPECIAL TOPIC: PROBLEMS AND LIMITATIONS OF HUMAN LANGUAGE

verses.zh: 「你们不可试探耶和华―你们的　神，像你们在玛撒那样试探他。
verses.en: You must not put the Lord your God to the test as you did at Massah.[NOTE:1]
notes: The place name Massah (מַסָּה, massah) derives from a root (נָסָה, nasah) meaning “to test; to try.” The reference here is to the experience in the Sinai desert when Moses struck the rock to obtain water (Exod 17:1-2). The complaining Israelites had, thus, “tested” the Lord, a wickedness that gave rise to the naming of the place (Exod 17:7; cf. Deut 9:22; 33:8).
verses.commentary:
6:16 "You shall not put the Lord your God to the test, as you tested Him
at Massah" The place was named "test," massah (BDB 650). This is a reference to an event that
happened in Exod. 17:1-7 ("tested" BDB 650, KB 702, Piel PERFECT), where the people
grumbled against God's provision and presence (cf. Deut. 9:22; 33:8). They showed lack of faith (cf. Ps. 95:8;
Hebrews 3-4). Do not do it again ("test" Piel IMPERFECT)!

This verse is also used by Jesus in His temptation experience with Satan (cf. Matt. 4:7; Luke 4:12).
Jesus quoted a Deuteronomy passage at every one of Satan's temptations.

verses.zh: 要留意遵守耶和华―你们　神所吩咐的诫命、法度、律例。
verses.en: Keep his[NOTE:1] commandments very carefully,[NOTE:2] as well as the stipulations and statutes he commanded you to observe.
notes: Heb “the commandments of the Lord your God.” The pronoun has been used in the translation for stylistic reasons to avoid redundancy.

The Hebrew text uses the infinitive absolute before the finite verb to emphasize the statement. The imperfect verbal form is used here with an obligatory nuance that can be captured in English through the imperative. Cf. NASB, NRSV “diligently keep (obey NLT).”
verses.commentary:
6:17 "You shall diligently keep the commandments of the Lord your God" See note
at Deut. 6:3. This continual emphasis on obedience (see note at Deut. 5:1) is overwhelming and sets the stage for the
covenant relationship. All of God's covenants with mankind are initiated by Him unconditionally, but faithful followers must
respond continually, daily (cf. Deut. 5:32, 33; 6:1, 2, 3, 17, 24, 25).

SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP

▣ "the commandments. . .His testimonies and His statutes" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: TERMS FOR GOD'S REVELATION.

verses.zh: 耶和华眼中看为正、看为善的，你都要遵行，使你可以享福，并可以进去得耶和华向你列祖起誓应许的那美地，
verses.en: Do whatever is proper[NOTE:1] and good before the Lord so that it may go well with you and that you may enter and occupy the good land that he[NOTE:2] promised your ancestors,
notes: Heb “upright.”
Heb “the Lord.” See note on the word “his” in v. 17.
verses.commentary:
6:18 There are three terms that qualify Israel experiences:

- "you shall do what is right" ‒ VERB, BDB 793 I, KB 889, Qal
PERFECT with waw, "do"

- "right" ‒ BDB 449 means "right" or "pleasing," cf. Exod. 15:26; Deut. 6:18; 12:25,28; 13:18; 21:9

- "good" ‒ BDB 373 II, used twice, "what is pleasing," cf. Gen. 16:6; Deut. 12:28 (BDB 375 III, Deut. 6:24)

- "that it may be well with you" ‒ BDB 405, KB 408, Qal IMPERFECT,
"be good," cf. Deut. 4:40; 5:16,29,33; 6:3,18; 12:25,28; 22:7

Notice that all three are found in Deut. 12:25,28. If Israel keeps the covenant requirements, YHWH
will bring prosperity and security (Leviticus 26; Deuteronomy 27-28)!

verses.zh: 照耶和华所说的，从你面前撵出你的一切仇敌。
verses.en: and that you may drive out all your enemies just as the Lord said.
verses.commentary:
6:19 "by driving out all your enemies from before you" God gave them the Promised Land ("by
driving out," BDB 213, KB 239, Qal INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT, cf. Gen. 15:16-21). He gave them
military victory, but Israel still had to prepare for battle and go out and fight. This is probably a good combination to
show the provision of God and the necessary faithful covenantal response (cf. Josh. 1-12).

verses.zh: 「日后，你的儿子问你说：『耶和华―我们　神吩咐你们的这些法度、律例、典章是甚么意思呢？』
verses.en: When your children[NOTE:1] ask you later on, “What are the stipulations, statutes, and ordinances that the Lord our God commanded you?”
notes: Heb “your son.”
verses.commentary:
6:20 This is the continuing emphasis on the spiritual, covenantal training of the children (see full note at Deut. 4:10).

The unusual aspect of this context (i.e. Deut. 6:20-33) is that the eyewitnesses were dead and
their descendants were telling the story. Therefore, this may have become a liturgical formula (i.e. "when your
children ask. . .you shall say. . .," Exod. 12:26,27; 13:14-15; Deut. 6:20-25; Josh. 4:6-7,21-24).

It is possible that Deut. 6:20-24 is one of several passages that recite Israel's faith journey
with YHWH, from the call of Abraham to the Exodus-Conquest (cf. Deut. 26:5-9; Josh. 24:2-13; Psalm 77; 78; 105; 136).

▣ to fear the Lord our God" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: FEAR (OT)

verses.zh: 你就告诉你的儿子说：『我们在埃及作过法老的奴仆；耶和华用大能的手将我们从埃及领出来，
verses.en: you must say to them,[NOTE:1] “We were Pharaoh’s slaves in Egypt, but the Lord brought us out of Egypt in a powerful way.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “to your son.”

Heb “by a strong hand.” The image is that of a warrior who, with weapon in hand, overcomes his enemies. The Lord is commonly depicted as a divine warrior in the Book of Deuteronomy (cf. 5:15; 7:8; 9:26; 26:8).
verses.commentary: 6:21 "with a mighty hand" See note at Deut. 4:34 and SPECIAL TOPIC: HAND.

verses.zh: 在我们眼前，将重大可怕的神迹奇事施行在埃及地和法老并他全家的身上，
verses.en: And he[NOTE:1] brought signs and great, devastating wonders on Egypt, on Pharaoh, and on his whole family[NOTE:2] before our very eyes.
notes: Heb “the Lord.” See note on the word “his” in v. 17.
Heb “house,” referring to the entire household.
verses.commentary:
6:22 This is referring to the ten plagues of Egypt. Each one of the plagues was a judgment against
one of the Egyptian gods. Apparently these plagues spanned a period of about eighteen months, if one assumes
there was some degree of natural phenomena involved. God could have delivered them much faster but it is
my personal belief that He was working with the Egyptians' faith as well as that of the Hebrews. The mixed
multitude which left Egypt contained some believing Egyptians.

SPECIAL TOPIC: SIGN (OT)

verses.zh: 将我们从那里领出来，要领我们进入他向我们列祖起誓应许之地，把这地赐给我们。
verses.en: He delivered us from there so that he could give us the land he had promised our ancestors.

verses.zh: 耶和华又吩咐我们遵行这一切律例，要敬畏耶和华―我们的　神，使我们常得好处，蒙他保全我们的生命，像今日一样。
verses.en: The Lord commanded us to obey all these statutes and to revere him[NOTE:1] so that it may always go well for us and he may preserve us, as he has to this day.
notes: Heb “the Lord our God.” See note on the word “his” in v. 17.
verses.commentary:

- for their good (BDB 375 III, cf. Deut. 6:18) always

- for their survival (BDB 310, KB 309, Piel INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT)

verses.en: We will be innocent if we carefully keep all these commandments[NOTE:1] before the Lord our God, just as he demands.”[NOTE:2]
notes: The term “commandment” (מִצְוָה, mitsvah), here in the singular, refers to the entire body of covenant stipulations.

verses.commentary:
6:25 "And it will be righteousness for us" As Abraham's initial faith/belief and subsequent obedience was
accepted by YHWH (cf. Gen. 15:6; Rom. 4) as "righteousness," so too, covenant obedience on the part of israel (cf. Deut. 24:13).

- "to observe" ‒ BDB 793, KB 889, Qal INFINITIVE, cf. Deut. 4:6; 5:1,15,27,32; 6:1,3,18,24,25. See note at Deut. 5:1

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary which means that you are responsible for your own
interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation.
You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of
the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

- How is chapter 6 related to the Ten Commandments?

- Why is there such an emphasis on obedience to the covenant?

- What is the significance of Deut. 6:4-6 and how does it relate to polytheism, henotheism and monotheism?

- What is the responsibility of believing parents toward their children?

- Explain the etymology and the Biblical use of the term "righteousness" in both its OT and NT focus.

This is a study guide commentary, which
means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the
five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation.
Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

- There has been some discussion among commentators as to whether chapter 6 forms a conclusion
to the Ten Commandments or the introduction to a section on expansion of the concepts presented in the
Ten Commandments. Because of Deut. 5:28-33 it seems obvious to me that we are beginning a new section
which emphasizes obedience.

SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP

- Many commentators have assumed that chapter 6 is an expansion of the first commandment which asserts the priority of YHWH in our lives.

- There is a continuing emphasis in this chapter on YHWH's original promises to Abraham in Genesis 12:1-3
and their fulfillment (cf. Deut. 6:1, 3, 10, 18, and 23).
